clue.text: Festive treat from black stag in mating season?

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencil grades
an animal in its mating season is lustful, or randy
a stag butts with its antlers, so it is playfully a butter

explanation.surface: A seasonal treat seems to come from a deer in the rut.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a venison dish; the question mark flags that a stag is whimsically 'one who butts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy butter is the sweet sauce served with Christmas pudding, a festive indulgence.

clue.text: AC/DC covering a Christmas staple? That's rum

indicators.note: one piece covering another means it wraps around it

parts.note: AC/DC is slang for bisexual, abbreviated BI
a card is sent by almost everyone at Christmas

explanation.surface: Fans of the rock band AC/DC might be startled to hear their heroes wrapped round a seasonal staple.
explanation.walkthrough: AC/DC is not the rock band here but old slang for bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacardi is a well-known brand of rum, so the specific names the general.

clue.text: A header from Vardy, cracking ball — come on!

indicators.note: a letter cracking a word breaks into it and sits inside

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: a header is the start of something, here the opening letter of the footballer's surname

explanation.surface: A football commentator urges on a Jamie Vardy header that cracks the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Jamie Vardy is an English striker; 'header' is not a goal but his initial V, which goes inside DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance is to move forward, the same sense as come on as an urging cry or a progression.

clue.text: Unknown quantity of diamonds and heroin around vessel

indicators.note: the two pieces placed around a third enclose it between them

parts.note: D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds
horse is street slang for heroin
Noah's ark is a vessel

explanation.surface: A drugs haul of gems and heroin is found packed around a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is satisfied by the diamonds and the heroin together, one on each side of the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark horse is a person whose abilities are not yet known, an idiom for an unpredictable contender.

clue.text: Hem in blouse's edging fixed

indicators.note: the edging of a garment is its border, so the outermost letters of the word

parts.note: something fixed is set

explanation.surface: A seamstress hems a blouse whose edging has been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hem in' looks like a sewing instruction but means surround.
explanation.definitionFit: To beset is to surround or harass on all sides, which is what to hem in means as a phrasal verb.

clue.text: Fit six-footer right in the middle

indicators.note: the insect and the letter are placed in the stomach word

parts.note: the tum, or tummy, is the middle of the body
an ant is an insect, and insects have six feet

explanation.surface: A very tall man is fit, standing right in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person but is an insect; 'the middle' is the stomach, TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit can be an outburst of temper, which is exactly a tantrum.

clue.text: Slippery, sinful individual steals credit card back

indicators.note: something stolen is taken in, so the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: Eve ate the forbidden fruit in Genesis

indicators.note: back indicates the word is read in reverse

parts.note: Visa is a brand of credit card

explanation.surface: A wicked person pockets a credit card, slippery customer that they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The sinful individual is the Eve of Genesis; 'back' makes ASIV.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone evasive avoids straight answers, so they are slippery and hard to pin down.

clue.text: Look, with VAT rising, pop star trembled

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a vat is a large tub
Cher is a pop singer
shook means trembled

explanation.surface: A pop star trembles as value added tax goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is not the tax but a container, TUB. Butcher's hook is Cockney rhyming slang: 'hook' rhymes with look, so 'have a butcher's' means have a look.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang a butcher's hook stands for a look, a glance at something.

clue.text: In France, a man runs free of clothes

parts.note: un is French for a
cove is old British slang for a man or chap
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A Frenchman runs naked through the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cove' is dated British slang for a man, as in 'a decent cove'.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncover something is to strip it of its covering, freeing it of clothes as a verb phrase.

clue.text: Glower as student group knocked over clock

indicators.note: knocked over means turned backwards, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: the NUS is the UK National Union of Students
to clock someone is to hit them, as is to lamp them

explanation.surface: Someone glares as a group of students punches a clock off the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' reads as scowl, but it is literally something that glows. 'Clock' and 'lamp' are both British slang for hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunlamp gives off light and heat, so it is literally a thing that glows.

clue.text: Stones hit bird, after suffering without milk

indicators.note: the bird comes after the suffering in the answer

parts.note: pain is suffering
a tit is a small songbird
black coffee or tea is served without milk

explanation.surface: Someone throws stones at a bird, having suffered a milkless cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' is not rocks but the Rolling Stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint It Black was a 1966 number-one single by the Rolling Stones.

clue.text: My cryptic hint for old port

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, suggesting the word is jumbled

explanation.surface: A solver exclaims at a puzzling hint about an ancient harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation, COR, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Corinth was an ancient Greek city with harbours on two gulfs, so an old port.

clue.text: Stops king donning transvestite's jacket and skirt

indicators.note: the king puts on the clothes, so they go around him
a jacket is an outer covering, so the outside letters of the word

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch wears a cross-dresser's jacket and skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are the end stations of rail or bus lines, the final stops.

clue.text: Base of trifle with less calorific cream

indicators.note: the base is the bottom, the final letter of the word

parts.note: lite labels a lower-calorie product

explanation.surface: A dessert recipe uses lighter cream at the bottom of the trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cream' looks like part of the trifle, but it means the best.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its finest part, a select group of the best.

clue.text: Lying bum flogged modern houses

indicators.note: one word houses another by holding it inside

parts.note: recent means modern

indicators.note: something flogged is beaten about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A dishonest layabout sells off new-build homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' suggests untruth but means lying down; 'flogged' suggests sold but makes UMB, and 'houses' does the inserting.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent means reclining or lying down, a formal synonym.

clue.text: European composer, in recital, has things to do

indicators.note: a recital is a performance spoken or played aloud, so the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: a Czech is a European; Franz Liszt was a composer

explanation.surface: A European composer has a long to-do list before a recital.
explanation.definitionFit: A checklist is a list of items to be done or verified, the tasks still pending.

clue.text: Clergies horrified about a deed such as this?

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes around the article
the clergy are thrown into disarray, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Priests are appalled by an act of desecration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrified' scrambles CLERGIES, which goes 'about' A. The definition leans on the surface: a deed that would horrify the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrilege is the violation of something sacred, the very act that would appal churchmen.

clue.text: Overcook pork pie and coke

parts.note: to char food is to burn it by overcooking
in Cockney rhyming slang a pork pie (porky) is a lie

explanation.surface: A cook burns a pork pie and serves it with a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coke' is not the drink but slang for cocaine; pork pie is rhyming slang for lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie is slang for cocaine, which is also called coke.

clue.text: Reluctance to move home, rate changes entrapping one

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: the jumbled word traps the numeral inside it
changes means the word is altered into a fresh order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Changes to the mortgage rate trap a homeowner who is reluctant to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrapping' puts I inside ERTA, the anagram of RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the tendency of a body or person to stay put and resist change.

clue.text: Tuck in to sample a treat

indicators.note: in to points inside the words that follow, where the answer sits

explanation.surface: An invitation to dig in and sample a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck in' looks like a phrase about eating; 'Tuck' alone is a fold.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold sewn into fabric, the same as a tuck.

clue.text: Rider favouring protection for face when cut

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: cut means shortened by losing its final letter

parts.note: a visor shields the face

explanation.surface: A horse rider wants protection for their face after being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' suggests a horseman, but it is a clause added to a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an added condition or qualification, which is what a proviso is.

clue.text: Theologian and Darwin swapping tips for theorem

indicators.note: swapping signals that one letter of the name is exchanged for another

parts.note: Erasmus Darwin was Charles Darwin's grandfather

indicators.note: the tips of the word are its ends; the opening one replaces the closing one, M

explanation.surface: A theologian and Darwin swap ideas about a theorem.
explanation.walkthrough: Theorem's tips are T and M; in ERASMUS the M becomes T. Thomas Erastus was a 16th-century Swiss theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Erastus was a Swiss theologian who argued the state should rule church matters.

clue.text: Equids, one of them hidden by rambling rose

indicators.note: the horse is concealed within the other letters
a rambling rose spreads untidily, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: a nag is a horse, one of the equids

explanation.surface: Horses hide behind a rambling rose in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' makes ORES, and 'hidden by' tucks the horse inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Onagers are wild asses of Asia, members of the horse family Equidae.

clue.text: Martial arts teacher's detailed wisdom

indicators.note: de-tailed means with the tail, its last letter, removed

parts.note: a sensei is a teacher of martial arts

explanation.surface: A martial arts master imparts detailed wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as thorough but means de-tailed, losing the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense is good judgement or practical wisdom, as in common sense.

clue.text: Smug fellow's not a boring tool, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks that the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: not a means no, none at all; an awl is a tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: A smug chap insists he is no dull tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' is not dull but drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is a person who smugly behaves as if they have all the answers.

clue.text: One's heavy, large and round, wearing clothes outside?

indicators.note: the clothing goes outside the other letters

parts.note: kit means clothes, especially sports gear
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
O is round in shape
to have something on is to be wearing it

explanation.surface: A large, round person with clothes on admits to being heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts KIT around LO.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiloton is a weight of a thousand tons, so one is heavy indeed.

clue.text: Silly graduate abandons speaking naturally

indicators.note: the graduate leaves, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: idiomatic language is how native speakers naturally talk
MA is a Master of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: A silly graduate gives up speaking in a natural way.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means foolish or stupid, the same as silly.

clue.text: Faulty gasometer in a kind of household

indicators.note: faulty means broken, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A broken gas meter in a home causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A ménage à trois is a domestic arrangement of three people living together as lovers.
